name: Dungan Mosque
near: Karakol; the mosque is in the city — 140–142a Abdrakhmanov St., at the corner of Bektenov St. (the central Ibrahim-azhy mosque).
elev: About 1700–1750 m (central Karakol lies at 1690–1770 m; calculated from the city's elevation, there are no point measurements for the mosque).
short: A wooden mosque in the Chinese pagoda style, built by the Dungans in 1907–1910 without a single nail — Karakol's main landmark and a working mosque.
desc: The Dungan Mosque was built by the Dungan community — Chinese Muslims who fled to Semirechye after the uprising of 1877. In 1907 the master Zhou Si arrived from Beijing with a team of ~20 carvers, roofers and masons; three years went into preparing materials, assembly took three months, and the mosque opened on 10 May 1910. The 27×15 m rectangular building of Tian Shan spruce, elm, poplar and walnut is assembled with grooves and tenons, with no nails; it has a multi-tiered roof with upturned corners, carved eaves with dragons, phoenixes and lions, and symbolic colours: red columns (protection from evil), a green roof (well-being), yellow details (wealth). In the 1930s the minaret was torn down and the mosque was closed, but the building survived; the minaret was restored a decade later. Today it is Karakol's working central Ibrahim-azhy mosque and one of the two surviving Dungan mosques in the former USSR.
guide: Walk to the rear of the courtyard — that gives the best angle on the tiered roof with upturned corners, which looks like a Buddhist temple; from the front, the fence and trees block the view. Look closely at the carving under the eaves: dragons, phoenixes and lions — Chinese mythology on a Muslim building, and not a single nail in 115 years. You aren't always let inside: it is a working mosque, and during prayer (especially on Friday 13:00–14:30) viewing is from outside only; women are given a robe and a headscarf at the entrance. Allow 15–20 minutes and combine it with the Holy Trinity Cathedral a kilometre away — two wooden churches of the same era. When you come out, head to the bazaar for ashlan-fu: it is a Dungan dish, and Karakol makes it best in the country.
see: The tiered pagoda roof and carved eaves with dragons and phoenixes; painted columns and beams; assembly without nails; the restored minaret; the courtyard with a garden; the women's section with a separate entrance.
skip: You aren't interested in architecture — viewing from outside takes 10–15 minutes, the grounds are small, and the interior is often closed. You're in Karakol on Friday at midday prayer — access is limited.
diff: Very easy: a city walk, entry from the street, steps at the entrance.
when: Year-round; in summer (June–September) there are more tourists and tours, in winter it's quiet. Avoid Friday prayer (13:00–14:30) and big holidays (Oraza Ait, Kurman Ait), when the mosque is packed.
hours: For tourists daily ~08:00–18:00 (Destination Karakol, undated); 2GIS gives no hours; entry inside depends on services — prayers on Fridays 13:00–14:30. Google Maps: “Daily: 24 hours” (as a working mosque).
daytime: Morning after 9:00 or around 18:00 (evening light on the facade; TripAdvisor reviews advise ~18:00 and hours without groups). Avoid 13:00–14:30 on Friday.
how: Karakol, 140–142a Abdrakhmanov St., at the corner of Bektenov St. — 10–15 minutes on foot from the central square and the bazaar; city marshrutkas (minibuses) (no. 109/111 and others, 20 som in 2024) and taxis (Yandex Go). From Bishkek to Karakol is ~400 km: marshrutkas from the new bus station (1/1 Alma-Atinskaya St.), the GoBus shuttle (450 som in 2022–2023), ~500 som by marshrutka (summer 2024), 6–7 h.
needcar: No — on foot around the city; a taxi is handy if your lodging is on the outskirts.
self: Yes: entry is free with a small fee/donation; follow the dress code (covered arms and legs, a headscarf for women — provided at the entrance), take off your shoes inside, don't photograph people praying.
roadtype: City streets of Karakol (paved) up to the Bektenov/Abdrakhmanov intersection; a pedestrian entrance into the courtyard through the gate.
traveltime: From the centre of Karakol 10–15 min on foot; viewing 10–20 min from outside, up to 30–40 min with a guided tour. Bishkek — Karakol 6–7 h by marshrutka (minibus).
stay: Karakol has dozens of options: guesthouses and hostels (budget ~1000–2000 som/person, 2024–2025 per reports), the “Turkestan” yurt camp in the city (karakol.kg), mid-range hotels; book via Booking/Destination Karakol. Check specific 2026 rates when booking.
net: Full Beeline, O!, MegaCom (4G) coverage in Karakol; Wi-Fi in guesthouses and cafes.
entry: A small fee to enter the grounds: 20–50 som (2GIS: 20–50 som, free for Muslims; a summer 2024 report — 50 som for the garden; Destination Karakol and TripAdvisor 2019 — 20 som). Sometimes a donation is requested. There is no official 2026 rate.
transfer: City marshrutka (minibus) 20 som (2024); Bishkek — Karakol marshrutka ~500 som (2024), GoBus 450 som (2022–2023); a taxi around the city — by the app's meter.
bring: A scarf and clothing that covers arms, legs and head (for women; hooded robes are provided at the entrance), shoes that are easy to take off, small cash (20–50 som), a camera — photos from outside are allowed, inside and of people — with permission.
warn: A working mosque: during prayer (Friday 13:00–14:30 and the five daily prayers) tourists are not admitted inside — the courtyard only. Observe the dress code and keep quiet. The entry fee is informal (20–50 som) — ask what you are paying for; sometimes they ask for money “for the children”. Don't confuse it with other mosques in Karakol — you want the Central Ibrahim-azhy mosque at 142a Abdrakhmanov.
food: Ashlan-fu — a Dungan cold noodle dish with starch jelly; in Karakol it is made at the Ak-Tilek bazaar and in cafes by the market (~90 som with flatbread, 2024); Dungan manti and lagman; local apricots and honey at the market.
reviews: Google Maps (“Dungan mosque”): 4.5/5, 1820 ratings as of 03.10.2026. 2GIS “Central Ibrahim Azhy Mosque”: 5/5, 311 ratings (07.10.2026). TripAdvisor “Dungan Mosque”: 3.9/5, 199 reviews, no. 6 of 40 in Karakol (07.10.2026). Pros: unique “Chinese” architecture, colours, quiet; cons: you're often not let inside, the grounds are small and cramped for photos, the visit is short, the entry fee is unclear.
p.sum: The mosque stands in the centre of Karakol (the corner of Abdrakhmanov and Bektenov streets), 10–15 minutes on foot from the square and the bazaar. The overnight GoBus from Bishkek (700 som) arrives at 05:40 right at the mosque. Entry to the courtyard is 20–50 som, open to tourists roughly 06:00–21:00 (Nomad's Land). On Friday 13:00–14:30 you aren't admitted inside. Allow 30–40 minutes for the visit. Combine it with the Holy Trinity Cathedral (1 km) and ashlan-fu in the “ashlan-fu row” at the bazaar. Stay in Karakol hostels from $7 in a dorm.
